correctness.rationale: For N(s,t)=max(|s|,|t|,|s-t|), I independently re-enumerated all six signed norm facets against six possible y edges after edge-transitivity fixes x=(1,u): solving N(x+y)=N(x-y) as piecewise affine equality with exact rational inequalities returns exactly eight nonempty segments (two each on y-edges 1,2,4,5). The repository's exact facet certificate additionally supplies explicit dihedral matrices identifying the two canonical families y=±((1-u)/2,1), 0<=u<=1/3. For lambda>=1 the facet lower envelopes cross at 2(1-u)/(1+u) and 2/(1-u); their derivative signs reduce the global infimum to crossings. The plus family is strictly above 32/45. For the minus family the sharp R(u)>=(32/45) reduces exactly to (3u-1)(15u^3-25u^2+56u-20)>=0 on [0,1/3]. The explicit unit isosceles pair x=(1,1/3), y=(-1/3,-1), lambda=3 attains N(x+3y)=8/3 and H2=3sqrt(10)/8. The lambda<1 case is obtained by interchanging the ordered unit pair and inverting lambda. This establishes the continuum theorem, not merely a finite sample; original audit and verifier scripts were inspected, not blindly executed.
